cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). It's preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, but some of them are saying something about the dead. I bet Paul's eyebrows went up higher than mine do when somebody asks for a cookie with NO chocolate chips.

cards.question: It's preached that Christ has been raised from the dead. What are some people in Corinth saying?

answers.text: There is no resurrection of the dead
Paul is not a real apostle

cards.question: Some in Corinth say there is no resurrection of the dead. Paul says that even then, Christ could still have been raised.

cards.text: So Paul follows that idea all the way out, like pulling one loose thread on a sweater, friend. If Christ has not been raised, two things become worthless right along with it.

cards.question: Paul says if Christ has not been raised, the apostles' ___ is worthless, and so is the Corinthians' ___.

cards.text: Now it gets personal for Paul. He and the others have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, and they put their NAMES on that, the way I put mine on every cookie box I seal.

cards.question: If the dead are not raised, what does Paul say that would make him and the others?

cards.text: Paul says it again: if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised. Some things you say twice, friend, like "that oven is HOT," and now he spells out what it would mean for the Corinthians.

cards.question: If Christ has not been raised, Paul tells the Corinthians their faith is ___.
And if Christ wasn't raised, where does Paul say that leaves the Corinthians?

cards.text: Then Paul thinks about the believers who have already died, and he calls them those who have fallen asleep in Christ. Now, I spent YEARS dozing in the back of a junk drawer, friend, but that is NOT the kind of sleep he's talking about.

cards.question: If Christ wasn't raised, Paul says those who have fallen asleep in Christ are simply resting safely.

cards.text: Then Paul zooms WAY out and puts himself in the picture: what if our hope in Christ is for this life alone? Picture buying the best seat in the house for a show, and finding out there IS no show.

cards.question: What does Paul say about believers if their hope in Christ is for this life alone?

answers.text: They should be pitied more than anyone
They should be envied more than anyone
They should be feared more than anyone

cards.text: Then Paul flips it: "But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep." SOMEBODY get this man a microphone!

cards.question: Paul calls the risen Christ the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. What does that picture point to?

answers.text: He is the first of many to be raised
He is the only one ever to be raised
He was the first person ever to die

cards.text: Paul takes it WAY back, friend, before ovens, before bakeries, before anybody ever said the word cookie. Death came through a man.

cards.question: Since death came through a man, Paul says the resurrection of the dead comes through the angels.
Paul says in ___ all die, and in ___ all will be made alive.

cards.text: That's Adam, the very first man (Genesis 2:7). And there's an order to it all, each in his own turn, like my oven, friend: the first batch comes out, THEN the next one.

cards.question: Christ goes first as the firstfruits. Who does Paul say comes next?

answers.text: Those who belong to Him at His coming
Everyone on earth the very next day

cards.text: Then the end will come. Christ destroys all dominion, authority and power, and hands over the kingdom to God the Father, and friend, I've got goosebumps all the way down my mustache.

cards.question: Paul says Christ must reign until something happens. Until what?

answers.text: Until all His enemies are under His feet
Until the temple is rebuilt in Jerusalem
Until the last apostle has died

cards.question: Paul says the last enemy to be destroyed is ___.

cards.text: Paul quotes Scripture (Psalm 8:6): "God has put everything under His feet." Clearly, he says, that everything doesn't include God, the One who put everything under Him, the same way when I say I packed EVERYTHING, I didn't pack myself in the cookie box.

cards.question: Paul says that when all things are subjected to the Son, the Son Himself will be made subject to God, so that God may be all in all.

cards.text: Paul comes at it from ANOTHER angle, and this man has more angles than Berry, and Berry is a STAR. He points to people who are baptized for the dead.

cards.question: Paul asks why people are baptized for the dead if the dead are not raised at all.

cards.text: Then Paul turns it on himself and the others: why would they put themselves in danger every hour? Every HOUR, friend, and my mustache starts shaking when the oven timer hits one minute.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians he faces death every ___.

cards.text: Me? I held my breath every time that junk drawer opened, scared it was cleanout day, and Paul faces death EVERY SINGLE DAY. Then he asks, "If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain?"

cards.question: If the dead are not raised, what way of living does Paul say might as well take over?

answers.text: Live it up since tomorrow we die
Work hard since the end is near
Stay quiet since no one is listening

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians the company they keep has no effect on their character.

cards.text: Then Paul rings a wake-up call so loud it would make Mags jealous. Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning.

cards.question: Why does Paul tell the Corinthians to sober up and stop sinning?

answers.text: Some of them are ignorant of God
Some of them are leaving the church
Some of them are too proud to pray

cards.text: Paul tells them, "I say this to your shame." But don't close the cookie box yet, friend, because he's not finished teaching on this.

findings.problem: Adam has not been mentioned or connected with death in any earlier card; he is identified only on the following card. With Moses, Abraham and Noah as alternatives, a baker relying on the earlier cards cannot reason out the first blank, making this a name-and-wording guess rather than a meaning-based blank.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This is a who question, but the wrong answer "Everyone on earth the very next day" is an invented group-and-time combination, not a real detail from somewhere else in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Sabbath" is arguable: facing death every day would include facing death on every Sabbath. It is therefore too close to the correct answer "day" and should be replaced with a clearly false option.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
